summary: The room covers basic Linux shell operations using the bash terminal.
It teaches how to navigate directories, list files, and read file contents.
Key topics include hidden files, file permissions with chmod, and calculating file hashes with md5sum.
It also explains common command flags like -h for human-readable output in df.

points.text: The terminal runs a shell (bash) that reads input and executes programs.
pwd prints the current folder path.
cd changes directory to a specified path.
ls -la lists all files including hidden ones in long format.
cat prints the contents of a file to the screen.
cat -l prints file contents with line numbers.
grep -i error searches for lines containing 'error' ignoring case.
find looks for files matching a name pattern and suppresses permission errors with redirect.
Files starting with a dot are hidden from a plain ls command.
chmod 600 sets permissions so only the owner can read and write the file.
md5sum prints a 32 character hex hash for a file or string.
The -h flag in df shows sizes in human-readable units like G and M.

concepts.name: Bash Shell
concepts.definition: The Bash shell is the interface that reads text typed into the terminal and executes corresponding programs or commands.
points: It acts as a bridge between the user and the operating system.

concepts.name: File Permissions
concepts.definition: Permissions control who can read, write, or execute a file. The chmod command changes these permissions using numbers (like 600) or symbols (+x).
points: chmod 600 restricts access to the owner only for reading and writing.
chmod +x adds execute permission to a file.

concepts.name: Hidden Files
concepts.definition: Files starting with a dot (.) are hidden by default and do not appear in a standard ls listing unless the -a flag is used.
points: They are useful for storing configuration files that shouldn't be seen by casual users.

concepts.name: File Hashing
concepts.definition: A hash like MD5 produces a fixed-length string (32 hex characters) representing the content of a file. It is used to verify if a file has been altered.
points: The output is a 32 character hexadecimal number.

concepts.name: Disk Usage
concepts.definition: The df command reports disk space usage. Using the -h flag displays sizes in human-readable units like Gigabytes (G) and Megabytes (M).
points: -h makes the output easier to read for humans.

claims.claim: The terminal runs a shell (bash here) that reads what I type and runs programs.
pwd print the folder I'm in
cd /var/log go into the logs folder
ls -la long list, including hidden files
cat -l notes.txt same but with line numbers
grep -i error app.log lines containing error, any case
find / -name '*.conf' 2>/dev/null look for config files, hide permission errors
Files whose names start with a dot are hidden from a plain ls.
chmod 600 means only the owner can read and write the file.
chmod +x backup.sh make the script runnable
md5sum prints a 32 character hex hash, e.g. for the word hello
Shows sizes in human-readable units like G and M

answers.answer: The -h flag tells the df command to display disk usage in human-readable formats (like GB or MB) instead of raw blocks.
